text: Data: a practice sky (simulation). The two pictures show the same color, so the comparison is fair (score 98 of 100). The color difference alone makes the star look 0.0 percent brighter. The pictures show it 2.6 percent brighter. No real change remains after the color effect is removed. The position measurements say: it moves. The motion is 4.67 plus or minus 0.02 arcseconds per year, from 66 pictures. The difference from the catalog value is 1.4 times the error. Summary: motion candidate. This is a candidate label and not a discovery.
